notes.title: 🚨Torn Apart Prototype out now!
notes.content:
After launching our first prototype “LEVEL 0: A Backrooms Experience” in March, we are now ready to unveil [b]our latest free-of-charge Steam prototype[/b]. In collaboration with the developers from [b]Monokel[/b] we have created a game about deception, accusation, denial, judgment, and zombies: [b]Torn Apart[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43994023/03c2153730601ee9f94443596720f8f2c4f86099.gif[/img]

This social deduction game is all about trying to survive – as either the (aptly named) survivors or the dastardly traitors. Download our prototype and stop the zombies from entering your base before you [b]discover which of your teammates have been secretly working against you[/b]!

This prototype is the most fun with 4-8 players, so make sure to get a few of your friends to download the game as well. Additionally, there are plenty of settings to play around with when creating a custom game, if you want more of a challenge (or if you just want to walk around the map really, [i]really[/i] fast).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43994023/6fcdcad1cb2d48b522a9a1d59b7d7cbaedb2e719.gif[/img]

Of course, [b]this is just a prototype[/b]. That means the ideas aren't fully developed yet, and some mechanics are still heavily simplified, while there's a lot of potential to explore.

This is where you come in. Try out this prototype, have fun with it, and [b]let us know what you think of "Torn Apart”[/b]. Would you play a full version? Maybe this theme doesn't appeal to you at all?

We would be immensely grateful if you could provide us with [b]feedback[/b]. Perhaps you even have some ideas for a potential full version. Please share them with us!

Join the conversation in the comments or in discussions on our [url=https://discord.gg/headupgames]Discord server[/url]. You can also give us your feedback [url=https://bit.ly/42XEqQS]via this form[/url]. We're looking forward to hearing from you!

We hope you have a great time with [b]Torn Apart[/b]!

Your team at Headup

notes.title: 🧟 Insight into Torn Apart: How it works
notes.content:
Hey there! 

Before [b]Torn Apart[/b] launches next week, we want to give you a quick overview of how the game works, so you're all set for your first rounds! Additionally, we will upload a guide we recommend you check out before getting started.

Your goal in Torn Apart is to protect your group’s camp from zombies and escape with the rescue helicopter that's on its way to you. To do that, you need to repair barricades and other defense systems to keep the zombies out. [b]Pressing "F" will bring up your radar[/b], which shows you all the places in the camp where things need to be repaired. But be quick! You only have limited time before the zombies storm your camp.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43994023/3da93cb2dc1d4c7351ae2c31172f43705cde2002.gif[/img]

You start the game in the meeting room where you'll find a table with tools. [b]Grab a hammer or screwdriver – it doesn't matter which one – and then explore the camp[/b]. When the alarm goes off, that means areas in the camp need to be repaired.

But here's the twist: one of you (or two, depending on your settings) will be a [b]Traitor[/b]. Their job is to eliminate all the other players before the helicopter arrives so that they can leave the camp alone (more legroom in the helicopter, amirite). The Traitor can [b]eliminate players by right-clicking with their tool[/b]. But beware! If someone catches you, they can call an Emergency Meeting where the group can vote to eject a player from the camp.

You can call an [b]Emergency Meeting[/b] in two ways: pressing the big button in the meeting room or finding a dead body and clicking on it. [b]You must go to the meeting room immediately when the meeting is called[/b]. You only have limited time to gather there. Only the players in the room can participate in the meeting, but everyone else can listen in from outside. The group can decide to eject a player from the camp, even if the chosen player is not part of the meeting.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43994023/e4900d22c3ad0ad40b9e547b8054cfd13df2b8d6.gif[/img]

If the Traitor is ejected from the camp, the survivors win. If the Traitor doesn't eliminate all the survivors before the helicopter arrives, the survivors win too. So, the Traitor needs to eliminate all the other players. Easy, right?

One last tip: Use the features of the camp to get rid of your fellow players "creatively". There are hidden spikes on the ground (fun), a shooting range (very fun), and pianos (maximum fun) that you can use to create "accidents." Whoopsies!

We hope you have a blast playing [b]Torn Apart[/b]. Be sure to check out our game guide which will be released right before the game becomes available. It should answer any further questions you have or any new ones that come up while you play!

Your Team at Headup

notes.title: 🧟 Insight into Torn Apart: Our Vision
notes.content:
Hi all! 

Today we want to tell you a bit more about the development of [b]Torn Apart[/b] and our vision for the prototype. From [b]May 22nd[/b], you will have the opportunity to download the free demo directly from our store page and play with up to eight players, accuse each other, defend against zombies, and just generally have a good time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43994023/b1d223ac7073b82a9c4ad91848da13acbcd2ccf6.gif[/img]

Our prototypes are created in two different ways. Our internal team of developers works on their own prototypes (more on that soon, we are currently in the process of figuring out which prototype to start with), and we also pick parallel studios that we know well, simply like or that deliver great games. In this case, all three checkboxes are ticked, because [b]Monokel[/b] developed our idea for us.

The process of creating such a prototype is relatively simple, but it also involves a lot of effort: First, someone has an idea. In the beginning, this is usually a sentence or simply a very short description. In this case: [b]"Does traitor gameplay work in first-person?"[/b] 

And that's where the work on Torn Apart began. 

The playtests were fun-filled, loud, and crazy evenings, during which Monokel's team, our team, and many friends and acquaintances thoroughly tested the gameplay. And let me tell you, even though our team is not known for consisting of the quietest and most reserved people anyway, this was on a whole new level: Accusations were constantly being made, and players were being thrown out of the camp (mostly innocent ones).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43994023/71232027a374f7c89e497438b1abbe8bf6f3022b.gif[/img]

We are so excited to be able to show you Torn Apart soon because we ourselves had the all too familiar [b]"One More Round" syndrome[/b].

What is super important to us (and we won't get tired of mentioning it over and over again): We need your feedback on Torn Apart! At the end of the day, we would love to produce a full version of this prototype, but we can't do it without your feedback. 

So please, message us on [url=https://discord.gg/headupgames]Discord[/url], the Steam forum, or on social media and let us know what you think of Torn Apart when it launches!

Your team at Headup

notes.title: Dr. Eva: How to survive a zombie apocalypse
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43994023/776ac9ac9e0665ffa303c535109c6b9fe67135b0.png[/img]

How would you survive in a zombie apocalypse, with a hidden traitor in your ranks? 

We know that our answer is - we wouldn't...

But fret not! In anticipation of Torn Apart launching May 22nd we hooked up with the actual live(!) zombie expert Eva Kingsepp to give us some invaluable tips for survival.

[b]So Eva, what is your relation to zombies anyway?[/b]

I used to watch lots of silly zombie movies in the 80’s, and when I began working on my PhD, which was about Nazi Germany/WWII in popular culture, I got into Nazi zombies, which became my niche regarding the undead. 

Some years ago I had watched almost all Nazi zombie movies available, but after Overlord (2018) I really got bored…

[b]Why are there zombies everywhere?[/b]

A good question! Why were they not that common in, say, the 1960’s? A simple explanation might be that since the 70’s the pop culture industry has grown to enormous proportions globally, not least through digital media - including games - and, of course, the internet. 

Besides this, the figure of the zombie itself has several dimensions that contributes to its popularity, including its usefulness as a metaphor (more about that below). However, most people who like zombies would probably simply say that they are fun - and that’s a very good explanation as well!

[b]What is your favorite depiction of zombies in fiction?[/b]

Hm, a difficult question. A good candidate would probably be the first Outpost movie (2008). 

[b]What do zombies stand for, are they a metaphor?[/b]

There is a popular idea about zombies being symbols, or a metaphor if you like, of consumer society. 

This idea has its origins in Romero’s satirical Dawn of the Dead (1978), but it’s not the only explanation to the popularity of the zombie phenomenon. Zombies are simply really excellent as symbols for lots of things that people find problematic or scary in today’s society, from mindless consumerism to global pandemics, nuclear war and other means for more or less bringing the world as we know it to an end. 

There’s an existential side to this as well: being undead, the zombie belongs to a dimension in-between life and death which challenges what we consider to be the natural order of things. The idea about the undead is found in several religions and cultures all over the world. 

Moreover, the zombie brings the dominant ideology of rationalism and science in contemporary society into question. I could go on bringing up other aspects as well, these are only a few.

[b]What are some of your best tips for working together as a group under severe zombie stress?[/b]

Keep calm and carry on.

[b]Can you give any advice on strategies for exposing a friend that is actually working for the zombies?[/b]

See how the person reacts when offered a piece of brain.

[b]Are the real zombies actually us? :O[/b]

Definitely!

notes.title: 🧟 Insight into Torn Apart: Prototyping
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

First of all: We're stoked to announce that you'll be able to try out our second prototype [b]Torn Apart[/b] from [b]May 22nd[/b]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43994023/a3142cc8fe2cfe163f197deec3787521ad245dad.gif[/img]

In Torn Apart, we're [b]experimenting with our own take on social deduction games[/b] by combining traitor gameplay with a first-person view.

We've had the idea of this mix brewing in our heads for a while now, so we're super happy to have found a studio like [b]Monokel[/b] that got our vision and executed it fantastically. Since we worked together on White Shadows, it was an easy choice for us to collaborate again and bring this prototype to life.

Through this new approach to "[b]prototyping[/b]", we have the opportunity to try out new ideas with you and test them directly, instead of spending ages figuring out whether they'll work. [b]We want to hear directly from you about what you think of our crazy ideas![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43994023/3da93cb2dc1d4c7351ae2c31172f43705cde2002.gif[/img]

So, we're counting on your feedback. From [b]May 22nd[/b], you can download the [b]free demo[/b] and play as much as you want with a group of up to eight players. Let us know if you like the prototype! What's fun and what can be improved? Would you play a full version of "Torn Apart", or is this free demo enough? Depending on your feedback, we'll either pursue more plans for the game or move on to the next awesome idea.

It's important for us to go on this journey together. After all, what's the point in us having fun with an idea that you aren't interested in playing? So, [b]please let us know what you think[/b]. You can visit us on [url=https://discord.gg/headupgames]Discord[/url] where our team is waiting to chat about prototyping, or drop by the Steam forum and share your thoughts there. We're also happy to hear your feedback on social media.

We hope you're excited to accuse each other in Torn Apart, survive the zombie apocalypse, or simply put your friends on the spot for no reason.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43994023/6fcdcad1cb2d48b522a9a1d59b7d7cbaedb2e719.gif[/img]

[i]Cos y’all already know that’s what this kinda gig is really all about.[/i]

Your team at Headup
